topic: Using Mutex for Thread Safety in C
explanation: A mutex, or mutual exclusion lock, is a synchronization mechanism in C that ensures only one thread can access a shared resource at a time. It is used to prevent race conditions in multi-threaded programs, where multiple threads might interfere with each other when modifying shared data, thereby maintaining data integrity and avoiding errors.
example_explanation: This program creates two threads that each increment a shared counter 10,000 times. The mutex is used to lock the critical section where the counter is modified, ensuring that only one thread can increment it at a time. This prevents race conditions, so the final counter value should be 20,000, demonstrating how the mutex protects the shared resource and maintains thread safety.
